name: Tata Communications

profile.address: 8343, Northeast Evergreen Parkway, Tanasbourne, Hillsboro, Washington County, Oregon, 97124
profile.reading: This Tata Communications facility sits on Northeast Evergreen Parkway in the Tanasbourne area of Hillsboro, Oregon, part of the Portland metro corridor known for chip manufacturing and telecommunications infrastructure. It carries the TGN designation, an abbreviation for the Tata Global Network, the name Tata Communications uses for the wholly owned undersea and terrestrial fiber system it built up around assets originally developed by Tyco Telecommunications. Hillsboro is not a coastal town, so this address most likely functions as an inland cable landing or terminating facility of the kind carriers use to bring a subsea cable's terminated fiber into a secure, road accessible building away from the immediate shoreline, before handing it off into terrestrial backhaul networks reaching Portland and beyond. As with Tata's other cable landing infrastructure, the company does not publish square footage, power capacity, or tenancy information for this specific site. That is consistent with how the submarine cable industry treats individual landing and terminating stations, which are typically described only in aggregate cable system documentation rather than as standalone real estate assets. No county permit or building record specific to this address was found in the course of this research. The facility should be understood as working carrier infrastructure supporting Tata's Pacific network reach, rather than a commercial, multi tenant data center.

reading: Tata Communications is a global telecommunications and network services provider headquartered in Mumbai, India, and a subsidiary of the Tata Group, one of India's largest conglomerates. The company operates one of the world's largest wholly owned subsea cable networks, marketed as the Tata Global Network, spanning roughly 500,000 route kilometers and connecting more than 190 countries. In the United States, Tata Communications operates cable landing stations that terminate segments of this network, including a facility in Hillsboro, Oregon, and the Wall Township, New Jersey cable landing station on the Jersey Shore, where Tata Communications leases carrier neutral meet me room space to NJFX. Tata Communications should be distinguished from its former data center and colocation joint venture business. In 2021, ST Telemedia Global Data Centres acquired Tata Communications' remaining stake in their jointly held Singapore data center business, meaning the branded colocation facilities that once carried the Tata Communications name in that market moved to STT GDC ownership. The submarine cable network and its US landing stations were not part of that transaction and remain core Tata Communications network infrastructure. A duplicate operator record in this registry, listed simply as Tata and tied to the Wall Township, New Jersey facility, refers to this same company and is linked here via duplicate_of rather than treated as a separate entity, since New Jersey press sources consistently identify the Wall Township cable landing station as a Tata Communications facility. No published critical IT megawatt figures were found for either US landing station, consistent with cable landing stations being network termination facilities rather than general purpose colocation data centers.
